edges.mechanism: Possible additive pharmacodynamic effects; high-dose MAO inhibitors combined with higher Cerebrolysin doses (>=30 mL) have been reported to increase blood pressure.
edges.evidence: Manufacturer treatment handbook (special warnings, based on SmPC) and FAQ; no controlled interaction study.

edges.mechanism: Possible additive effects with antidepressants; manufacturer recommends considering a lower antidepressant dose if psychiatrically safe.
edges.evidence: Manufacturer treatment handbook and FAQ; no controlled interaction study.

edges.mechanism: Listed contraindication (epilepsy in Austrian SmPC summary; status epilepticus in treatment handbook). Handbook states post-stroke/TBI seizures in non-epileptic patients are not a contraindication.
edges.evidence: Official prescribing information summary (Austrian SmPC) and manufacturer handbook.

edges.mechanism: Listed contraindication; handbook specifies no use at GFR categories 4 and 5.
edges.evidence: Official prescribing information summary (Austrian SmPC) and manufacturer handbook.

edges.mechanism: Product is a porcine brain-derived peptide preparation; hypersensitivity to any component is a labelled contraindication (application to porcine-protein allergy is an inference).
edges.evidence: SmPC summary contraindication plus Cochrane description of porcine origin; no case series of porcine-allergy reactions found.

edges.mechanism: Cochrane meta-analysis found no mortality benefit and an increase in non-fatal serious adverse events, more prominent with 30 mL x 10 days.
edges.evidence: Cochrane SR 2023 (RR non-fatal SAE 2.39, 95% CI 1.10-5.23; moderate certainty), consistent with 2017 and 2020 versions; a separate 12-RCT safety MA found no excess.

edges.mechanism: Rapid IV bolus is associated with increased heart rate, blood pressure and arrhythmia; blood pressure rise reported with high-dose MAO inhibitor co-use. Slow infusion (30-45 min per 100 mL) advised.
Co-administration with rt-PA studied; no excess adverse events and lower symptomatic haemorrhagic transformation reported; post hoc data hypothesise earlier stabilisation of HT hazard.
edges.evidence: Placebo-controlled RCT (n=119) and open-label RCT CEREHETIS (n=341; sHT OR 0.248); safety review; post hoc analysis is hypothesis-generating.

edges.mechanism: Neurotrophic plus cholinergic mechanisms; combination with donepezil was safe and gave best cognitive scores, without significant between-group cognitive differences.
edges.evidence: RCT (n=197) of Cerebrolysin, donepezil and combination; safety review covering donepezil/rivastigmine.

edges.with: IV amino acid solutions, vitamins and cardiovascular drugs (same infusion)
edges.mechanism: Pharmaceutical incompatibility: Cerebrolysin should not be mixed in the same infusion with balanced amino acid solutions, vitamins or cardiovascular products; they may be given separately.
Co-administered as background therapy in CASTA and a vascular dementia RCT without a specific interaction signal; manufacturer reports no incompatibilities with aspirin, statins or NOACs.
edges.evidence: Large RCTs (background therapy, not an interaction study) and manufacturer FAQ.

edges.mechanism: Both proposed neuroprotective/neurorestorative agents; combination tested in severe TBI.
edges.evidence: Retrospective cohort (n=80): non-significant trend favouring citicoline plus Cerebrolysin over citicoline alone; narrative review of combined use. Synergy unproven.

edges.mechanism: Theoretical concern that Sonic hedgehog pathway amplification could accelerate NAFLD progression; in stroke patients with raised transaminases AST improved in most.
edges.evidence: Single translational study (clinical case data plus mouse model); low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Only small trials in preterm infants and children with cerebral palsy; manufacturer cites infant use only as experience reports.
edges.evidence: Small open RCTs and narrative review; very low certainty.
